title: Newly eligible samples can miss an analysis rerun
fact: The dependency gate intersects changed sample IDs with baseline sample_ids. Only added/new_duplicate changes get a separate eligibility check. A clinical label change on an existing, previously excluded sample therefore does not trigger the rerun, even when the changed column is used by the analysis.
observed: A reviewer-authored group-A count changed S2 from group B to A. Direct recomputation returned n=2, but evaluate_analyses returned affected=false, status=not_rerun, after=null and a reason claiming no change touches the analysis. The baseline count was n=1.
impact: A release can change who belongs in an analysis while the tool reports that analysis as unaffected. This undermines the central promise of rerunning affected analyses. The probe establishes the generic dependency-routing defect; it does not establish its incidence in the event’s protected analyses.
fix: Treat changes to eligibility/filter columns as relevant across the candidate population, including rows absent from the baseline result. Prefer explicit analysis dependencies; conservatively rerun when membership cannot be proven unchanged.
accept: Change an excluded row so it meets the analysis filter; require a rerun, updated membership, and a reason linking the changed field. Also retain an unrelated-column negative control.

title: Duplicate clinical IDs disappear before comparison
fact: The row loader drops duplicate index values with keep="first" before building sample lists and fingerprints. Matrix loaders also retain only the first occurrence of each header ID (lines 122–125 and 151–155).
observed: Appending a conflicting S1 clinical row changed the file hash, but load_release retained two rows and diff_releases returned an empty change list. The original first row was unchanged.
impact: Identity and join defects are erased from the representation consumed by the detector. A changed file hash remains available, so this is not a claim of byte-identical releases. The specific defect is the absence of a duplicate-ID finding.
fix: Validate key uniqueness before normalization. Preserve duplicate counts, row positions and conflict summaries; emit a material identity finding and keep affected analyses unresolved until a reviewer chooses a deduplication policy.
accept: Append both identical and conflicting duplicate IDs; require explicit duplicate findings. Add duplicate matrix headers as a separate regression case.

title: Release approval can omit signed-result evidence
fact: tower_binding signs only question plus analysis IDs/verdicts (lines 35–39). review_release derives required acknowledgments from the submitted findings and affected_by arrays, which are not in that binding. Certificate creation uses the same binding in tower/findings.py:285–291.
observed: For a locally signed synthetic Conditional result, approval without acknowledging F1 was rejected. Removing findings and affected_by while retaining the same valid certificate made approve_with_conditions succeed with an empty acknowledgment list. The resulting review signature verified.
impact: A client can obtain a cryptographically valid review record without the evidence acknowledgment the original result required. This does not bypass the Blocked-verdict restriction or forge the signing key.
fix: Bind the full canonical evidence document, including finding IDs, affected_by, analysis outputs, repairs and release identity; or load the immutable server-side result by certificate ID. Reject any changed document before review.
accept: Mutate each protected evidence field independently after certification; all review requests must be refused. The original Conditional result must remain approvable with the required acknowledgments and note.

title: Question approval can record an unbound question
after:
Submitted question B
Valid signed approval
fact: review_question correctly takes verdict and rule IDs from the signed certificate, but takes the recorded question text from result.spec without recomputing and checking spec_sha256. The engine signs the canonical spec at engine.py:70–72.
observed: A valid certificate created for an original synthetic question was submitted with a different question_text. Approval succeeded, stored the changed question, and verify_review returned true.
impact: The audit trail can attach a valid approval to question text not covered by that certificate. The probe exercises the review function directly; an HTTP/browser exploit was not run.
fix: Resolve the canonical question spec from an immutable server record, or hash the received canonical spec and compare it with the signed spec_sha256 before accepting a review.
accept: Changing question_text, intended_use, filters or feature_columns after certification must reject the review; unchanged canonical input must still work.

title: Malformed inputs escape the safe fallback
before:
Bad JSON shape
Invalid numeric filter
fact: The engine catches SpecError, but _short_circuit assumes spec has .get (line 136). Dictionary access at line 62 assumes an object. run_checks catches a bad comparison, but build_funnel repeats the same filter outside that protection.
observed: A nonempty list spec and a nonempty list dictionary each raised AttributeError. A numeric column compared with a string using > raised TypeError. In contrast, an empty CSV returned INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, confirming a working fallback for that input class.
impact: Expected user mistakes can terminate evaluation instead of producing a usable Insufficient Evidence result. api/main.py:60–90 decodes JSON without validating object shape, so these shapes can reach the engine; HTTP status behavior is source-based inference, not a reproduced API test.
fix: Validate top-level and nested shapes at the boundary, enforce filter type compatibility, and make fallback formatting type-safe. Isolate funnel failure so an otherwise valid failure report can still return.
accept: Cover nonobject JSON, invalid column metadata, incompatible comparisons, and malformed filters; each must return a structured validation result without uncaught exceptions.

title: The sample export overstates complete cases
after:
2 complete cases
Both exported as yes
fact: build_funnel removes "*" instead of expanding the same feature set as checks._resolve_features. It also skips absent required fields and still writes can_answer_question=yes for retained rows. A missing-feature warning exists in not_in_data, which is useful but contradicts the row-level export.
observed: With feature_columns=["*"], a two-row input with one missing x value returned n_final=2 and two yes rows. With an explicitly absent predictor, it again returned two yes rows while listing the missing column in not_in_data.
impact: Users downloading the sample list can treat incomplete records as able to answer the question. This finding concerns the funnel/export; it does not claim the overall policy verdict is Ready.
fix: Share one resolved feature/eligibility definition between checks and funnel. For absent required fields, mark eligibility unknown/unavailable rather than yes; distinguish potential cohort membership from complete cases.
accept: Wildcard and equivalent explicit feature lists must produce identical retained IDs. A missing required predictor must never export all rows as answerable.

title: The optional wording guard accepts contradictions
fact: report_passes_guard checks verdict substrings, required IDs for Blocked/Insufficient Evidence, and an alternate verdict marker on the first line. It does not constrain the advice that follows.
observed: A synthetic string containing “Blocked [SCOPE]” followed by advice to ignore the warning and use the dataset for direct patient care returned true. No LLM request was made; this tests only acceptance of a supplied string.
impact: Optional generated wording can conflict with the deterministic result while passing the guard. The default template path is unaffected, and no claim is made that a live model produced this text.
fix: Keep verdict, safety statement and remedies in immutable template sections. Restrict generated content to a clearly labeled explanatory field that cannot replace authoritative instructions; default to templates on validation failure.
accept: Reject contradiction and negation fixtures, including advice after the required tokens. Verify the standard deterministic report remains available without model credentials.
